question: Can an opposite-token complete-set execution path improve loss control beyond selling the chosen token without repeating the classification failures of prior lifecycle exits?

prior_lifecycle_evidence.diagnosis: Both executable exits improved tail PnL but turned eventual winners into realized losers. An opposite-token ask may change execution payoff and liquidity, but it does not by itself solve the causal classification error.

research_contract.next_required_data: Fresh exact post-entry paired top-of-book paths with visible depth, book age, measured latency, fees, and terminal official-source labels.
comparison: opposite-token visible-ask full-size FOK purchase forming a complete set
research_contract.evaluation_rule: Replay both executable paths at unchanged preregistered lifecycle horizons and triggers; fail closed on stale books or insufficient displayed depth.
research_contract.anti_tuning_rule: Do not search adjacent horizons, trigger PnL values, latency values, or book-quality thresholds after observing outcomes.
research_contract.promotion_boundary: No hedge or exit rule may enter a strategy candidate until it avoids harmed winners on holdout data, improves the full exact-replay contract, and repeats on the freshest fully resolved window.

verdict.measurement_adjustment: paired executable-book state is now preserved for future causal replay
verdict.reason: The alternate execution route is technically distinct and worth measuring, but current evidence does not show that it can identify losses without exiting future winners.
verdict.grade: A- research system; A+ strategy remains unproven
